subject: Request: KMS-attributed latency carveout for private deployment (Terramara Health)
messages:
From: Jessica Li <jessica.li@terramara.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@terramara.io
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Performance: KMS-induced latency on private deployment

Hi Hannah,

We started seeing higher tail latency on our private deployment in us-west-2 after switching to our customer-managed KMS configuration last week. Sample traces attached show a consistent ~250-600ms add-on to request/response times (99th percentile). Our integration is sensitive to token-level latency and this is pushing us outside the 99th percentile latency commitment in the contract (150ms).

We are currently debugging internally — suspect the KMS calls (synchronous decrypts) are routed through a shared proxy and intermittently taking hundreds of ms. Until we can fully migrate KMS to a regional key in us-west-2 (work scheduled but takes time), we need Redwood to exclude KMS- or other customer-controlled infrastructure-induced latency from the SLA.

Specifically we are requesting: 
- A temporary carveout that latency attributed to customer-managed KMS, on-prem proxies, or CDN third parties will not be counted against Redwood latency SLOs for the private deployment in us-west-2.
- A narrow exception window (45 days) while we perform migration and validation; we can provide traces/logs during that time.

Can you share the contract language your side would accept for this? Also let us know what evidence you need from our side (traces, packet captures, KMS audit timestamps).

Appended: kms_latency_samples.csv (excerpt).

Thanks,
Jessica Li
Director of Cloud Ops
Terramara Health

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Li <jessica.li@terramara.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance: KMS-induced latency on private deployment

Jessica — thanks for the quick heads up and for attaching the sample traces. We appreciate the detail; that helps a lot.

Short version: we are open to a targeted carveout for third-party customer-managed services (KMS, on-prem proxies, customer-owned CDN) when we can demonstrate the added latency is not caused by Redwood’s serving runtime. We’ll need time-bound evidence and mutually agreeable language.

What we need from you to move fast: 
- Time-stamped traces (request IDs + server-side spans) showing KMS call latencies correlated to the end-to-end request.
- A short description of your KMS topology (regional vs. cross-region, proxies, vendor).
- Packet captures or traceroutes for a few incidents if possible (we don’t need large dumps, just representative captures).

Immediate mitigations we can offer while you migrate: 
- Configure prefix (KV) caching for non-sensitive flows to reduce KMS hits.
- Enable regional routing to prefer us-west-2 nodes (we can pin your traffic to avoid cross-region hops).
- A test to try Redwood-managed KMS for a subset of requests (we can run this in a controlled window).

I’ve attached a draft exception clause and an amendment template (redwood_proposed_exception_draft.docx) — treat as starting language. I’m looping in Monica to propose a technical runbook and Aditya to help with the legal wording.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the evidence and agree a temporary carveout timeline?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_proposed_exception_draft.docx
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Terramara KMS carveout — action items

Aditya / Monica — summarizing the ask from Terramara (copied from thread above): they are seeing 250-600ms tail latency attributable to their customer-managed KMS chained through a proxy. They want a 45-day carveout while they migrate to a regional key.

Aditya: can you draft a concise amendment that: 
- Excludes latency directly attributable to customer-managed third-party services (explicitly call out KMS, customer proxies, and customer-owned CDN) from Redwood’s latency SLOs for the duration of the exception; 
- Requires Terramara to provide incident traces + KMS audit timestamps for correlation; 
- Includes a sunset date and a requirement to confirm remediation (migration to regional KMS) or renegotiate if extended.

Monica: please propose a short mitigation playbook we can run in the interim — minimum viable approach: enable regional routing, prefix caching, and a supervised trial of Redwood-managed KMS (read-only or skewed traffic) during a 2-hour maintenance window. Also prepare the minimal instrumentation we need from Terramara (span IDs, request IDs, sample traceroutes).

I’ll schedule a 30m call for 06/13 14:00 PDT with customer. Keep it tight — we want language + runbook agreed in that call if possible.

Thanks — Hannah

From: Jessica Li <jessica.li@terramara.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@terramara.io
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance: KMS-induced latency on private deployment

Hannah — thanks for the quick turnaround and for looping in Aditya and Monica. Per our call, attaching the evidence we discussed:
- terramara_kms_latency_report.pdf (99th percentile traces + KMS audit timestamps)
- network-traceroutes-20280610.zip (traceroutes from our edge proxies to Redwood us-west-2 endpoints)

We are comfortable with the 45-day exception window while we migrate to a regional key and will provide the requested traces during the period. Please share the finalized amendment and a short checklist of what you need for the evidence correlation.

We are also open to the supervised test of Redwood-managed KMS; please propose a date/time next week (we prefer Tue/Wed mornings PT).

Appreciate your help — Jessica
Director of Cloud Ops
Terramara Health

Attachments: terramara_kms_latency_report.pdf, network-traceroutes-20280610.zip
